statement: Smithsonian NMAI's Haudenosaunee educational materials explain the Gayanesshagowa (Great Law of Peace) as guiding political and social life and describe clan mothers' responsibilities in leadership, ceremonies and community welfare.

sources.citation: Smithsonian NMAI, Native Knowledge 360, 'American Revolution: Haudenosaunee Perseverance', Chapter 5, 'The Practice of Peace', glossary and introductory description, https://americanindian.si.edu/nk360/american-revolution-perseverance/students/chapter-5/
sources.author: National Museum of the American Indian
sources.access_note: Full public educational chapter opened and read for Great Law and clan-mother definitions; no date of origin is asserted.

does_not_demonstrate: This educational description does not establish a founding year for the Haudenosaunee Confederacy.
Ceremonial, political and social authority are intertwined, and should not be flattened into a single doctrinal religion.
NMAI public teaching is not a literal transcript of every council's oral legal tradition.
adversarial_counter: Different Haudenosaunee nations and knowledge custodians may use distinct emphases; precise chronology requires separate dated evidence.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
